name: Grade 6 T1: Scratch Variables
description: Scratch game vocabulary for sprites, scripts, variables, values, scores, and debugging.

words.definition: A block-based programming tool used to make stories, animations, and games.
words.example: The class used Scratch to create a score challenge.

words.definition: A character or object in a Scratch project.
words.example: Each sprite changed the score by a different amount.

words.definition: The background area where a Scratch project runs.
words.example: The sprite moved across the stage.

words.definition: A coding instruction in Scratch that can be snapped into a script.
words.example: The student used a block to change the score.

words.definition: A group of connected blocks that tells a sprite what to do.
words.example: The script ran when the sprite was clicked.

words.definition: Something that starts code, such as a click or key press.
words.example: The click event changed the score variable.

words.definition: A named place in a program that stores a value that can change.
words.example: The score variable remembered the player's points.

words.definition: The information or number stored in a variable.
words.example: The value of score changed from 0 to 1.

words.definition: A number that tracks points in a game or challenge.
words.example: The score increased when the player clicked the correct sprite.

words.definition: To make a value become different.
words.example: The block changed the score by 5.

words.definition: To make a number or value larger.
words.example: Clicking the star increased the score.

words.definition: To make a number or value smaller.
words.example: Clicking the wrong sprite decreased the score.

words.definition: To set something back to its starting value or state.
words.example: The reset block set score back to 0.

words.definition: A rule that can be true or false in a program.
words.example: The game checked a condition before adding points.

words.definition: The order in which instructions run.
words.example: The sequence set the score, waited, and then changed the score.

words.definition: To find and fix a problem in code.
words.example: The student debugged the game when the score did not change.

words.definition: To run a project to check whether it works correctly.
words.example: The class tested each score task before submitting it.

words.definition: A small project made to practice one or two skills.
words.example: The Scratch score challenge was a mini-project.
